evidence_tree.method: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.

Effects that reduce the target's effective resistances before mitigation: percent penetration applies before flat penetration, results cannot go below 0, and only resistance reduction effects can drive armor/MR negative.

The game applies, in order: flat reduction → percentage reduction → percentage penetration → flat penetration ... reduce_resistance(R, r_flat, r_pct): R ← R − r_flat; R ← R·(1 − r_pct/100) ... R_final = max(0, (R − r_flat)·(1 − r_pct/100)·(1 − p) − f)

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

step_1_magnitude.rule: Carve: 6% armor reduction per stack, max 5 stacks (cached wiki text, 3071).
step_1_magnitude.result: fraction 0.30 is exactly the cached wiki cap; the old leaf's fraction is correct and no other Carve magnitude is reachable.

step_2_who_benefits.rule: Carve is armor *reduction*, not armor *penetration*. Both the item text ('Each stack inflicts 6% armor reduction' - it inflicts on the target, it does not let the holder ignore armor) and the wiki-atom definition ('Effects that reduce the target's effective resistances before mitigation') make it a debuff that lowers the target's armor stat itself.
step_2_who_benefits.corroboration: docs/math-foundations.md § 2.2 splits the pipeline exactly along this line: reduce_resistance(R, r_flat, r_pct) mutates the target's resistance R, while apply_armor_penetration(R, f, p) is applied per damage instance for the attacker holding the pen. Reduction lives on the target (team-wide); penetration lives on the attacker (personal). § 2.1 adds that only reduction can push R negative - a target-state property, not an attacker-state one.
step_2_who_benefits.conclusion: A Carve shred on the enemy applies to every damage source hitting that enemy, including an ally support's damage. The support's resistance-reduction ledger therefore SHOULD carry a 'Black Cleaver - Carve' entry while stacks are up; deleting it removes a legitimate team-wide shred.

step_3_factor_check.rule: m(R) = 100/(100+R) (§ 2.1). Amplification from a p-fraction armor reduction on a target with pre-reduction armor A is m(A(1-p))/m(A) = (100+A)/(100+(1-p)A).
check_table: A=125, p=0.30 -> 1.2000  (exact match to the old leaf)
step_3_factor_check.conclusion: The old pair (fraction 0.30, factor 1.2) is internally exact under the engine's own documented m(R) identity for a 125-armor target: 225/187.5 = 1.2. It is arithmetically self-consistent, not a stale literal. The 4-stack average model (§ 2.3 item 2, 0.8 x max_stacks = 24%) would have produced factor 1.1538, so the leaf was recorded from the exact 5-stack cap, which is what the wiki text licenses.

independent_computation.conclusion: Both components of the old leaf reproduce independently: fraction 0.30 = 5 x 6% from the cached Carve text, and factor 1.2 = (100+125)/(100+87.5) from the § 2.1 mitigation identity. Because armor reduction is a target-side debuff, the entry belongs in the support participant's ledger. The new value (absent) drops a real, correctly-valued effect.

residual_uncertainty.note: The scenario definition lives outside the permitted evidence tree (src/, tests/, scripts/), so this oracle cannot see the other four entries of support_resistance_reduction, the roster's champions, or the target's armor. Two alternative readings would make the deletion correct, and neither is checkable from data/ or docs/math-foundations.md:
alternatives: (a) index [4] was an exact duplicate of an earlier Carve entry already present at [0..3] (double-counted shred) - removing the duplicate would then be right, but the surviving entry's fraction must still be 0.30;
(b) the support's damage in this roster is entirely magic, in which case an armor_reduction_percent amplifier on it would be misapplied.
residual_uncertainty.why_verdict_stands: Neither alternative is supported by anything in the permitted sources, and reading (b) is contradicted by the roster's own support item: Bloodsong's Spellblade deals bonus *physical* damage on-hit, so the support does have an armor-mitigated damage component. On the evidence available, the leaf's value is right and its presence is right.
